annotations.title: Names and relationships
annotations.text: Several names in the opening are still phonetic machine readings. They remain unresolved until checked against the audio and family records.

annotations.title: Cheder
annotations.text: At about 00:05:00, the recognizer writes “Haida.” Abe is describing cheder, the traditional Jewish elementary school where boys began religious study.

annotations.title: Nadn
annotations.text: At about 00:08:00, Abe explains the Yiddish word nadn: the dowry or marriage portion associated with a match.

annotations.title: Place names
annotations.text: Machine variants such as Krasenbord, Samish, Tomshof, and Tomaschow likely refer to Krasnobród, Zamość, and Tomaszów Lubelski. The draft preserves the spoken evidence pending close listening.

annotations.title: The doctor
annotations.text: At about 00:24:00, Abe describes a Russian Jewish physician who was an Austrian prisoner of war and visited homes during an epidemic.

annotations.title: Language
annotations.text: The conversation is mostly English with Yiddish, Polish, and Yinglish words. Unfamiliar words are retained phonetically rather than replaced with guesses.
